title: Build and release: every tag publishes heca for every system
description: Approved by Antonio 2026-11-18. heca has CI (P?/T555: build, clippy, tests on macOS, Linux, Windows — .github/workflows/ci.yml) but no release: nothing builds downloadable binaries, and README says "no prebuilt downloads yet". This phase adds a release workflow: on every version tag, GitHub builds heca for every system and publishes zip archives and installers in a GitHub Release. Out of scope for now (recorded as an idea): Homebrew, AUR, winget/Chocolatey, code signing and notarization.

tasks.title: Release workflow: every v* tag builds heca for all systems and publishes zips and installers
tasks.description:
Agreed with Antonio 2026-11-18.

- TRIGGER: every tag `v*` (e.g. v0.1.0). The workflow checks that the tag equals the version in Cargo.toml (workspace version, Cargo.toml:6, today 0.1.0) and fails with a clear error if not.
- SYSTEMS: all — macOS Apple Silicon + Intel, Linux x86_64 (ARM if it does not complicate), Windows x86_64.
- PUBLISHES a GitHub Release with, per system: a zip (tar.gz on Linux) holding the binary, LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE and README; and installers — .dmg on macOS, .msi on Windows, and on Linux BOTH a .deb and an AppImage (Antonio, 2026-11-18).
- NO signing / notarization for now. The release page explains how to open an unsigned app on macOS ("unidentified developer") and Windows (SmartScreen).
- DOCS: README "Download" section; docs/development.md "How to release"; AGENTS.md gets a "Release" section stating that a new version is published ONLY by pushing a tag vX.Y.Z equal to the Cargo.toml version (written when the workflow exists, so it is true).
- VERIFY: a test release from a tag like v0.1.0-rc1; Antonio downloads and installs at least on macOS; then the test release is deleted.
- Out of scope (idea I025): Homebrew, AUR, winget/Chocolatey; signing/notarization.
- Existing CI to reuse: .github/workflows/ci.yml (T555), Linux system packages pkg-config libasound2-dev libssl-dev.

STEP 1 DONE (2026-11-18) — FINDINGS:
- heca is ONE self-contained binary (package `heca`, heca/Cargo.toml): fonts (heca-grid-ui/src/font.rs:31,35,56; heca-renderer/src/font.rs:21,25), sounds (heca/src/audio/assets.rs), default config/keybindings (heca-config/src/loader/mod.rs), shell-integration snippets (heca/src/app/backend_factory.rs:21-23) and agent assets are embedded with include_bytes!/include_str!. The server is the same binary (`heca --server`). Installers carry only the binary.
- cargo-dist (axodotdev.github.io/cargo-dist/book/installers): tarballs/zips, msi, shell/powershell scripts, homebrew, npm. NO dmg (listed as future), NO deb, NO AppImage.
- cargo-packager (github.com/crabnebula-dev/cargo-packager): macOS .dmg + .app; Linux .deb, AppImage, Pacman (tar.gz + PKGBUILD); Windows .msi (WiX) + .exe (NSIS). Its README does not say whether each format must be built on its own OS — verify in the test release.
- PROPOSAL (awaiting Antonio's approval): cargo-packager for all installers; zips/tar.gz made by a workflow step. Workflow shape: tag v* → version check → matrix build on GitHub runners (macOS arm64, macOS x86_64, ubuntu x86_64, windows x86_64) → cargo-packager per OS + archive step → upload all to the GitHub Release of the tag with the unsigned-app note. The PKGBUILD output is reusable later for AUR (I025).
Worktree: /Users/antonio/projects/heca-feat-566 (branch feat/t566-release-workflow).
tasks.notes:
STATE ON 2026-11-19. DONE and on main: .github/workflows/release.yml (tag v* → version check → build for aarch64/x86_64 macOS, x86_64 Linux, x86_64 Windows → cargo-packager installers + archive step → GitHub Release) — commits f6abfe88, ba4c39f8, 5a3c7feb, 73034bae (PR #324), transparent icon PR #325; cargo-packager config heca/Cargo.toml [package.metadata.packager]; docs: README "Download" (:36), docs/development.md "Releasing" (:59, numeric pre-release v0.1.0-1, not -rc1), AGENTS.md "Release". Test release v0.1.0-1 (pre-release, 2026-11-19) published with all 9 artifacts (zips for both Macs and Windows, Linux tar.gz, both .dmg, .deb, AppImage, .msi); Antonio installed it on macOS from the .dmg (his findings are T567).
LAST STEP (Antonio 2026-11-19: finish T566 first): macOS ad-hoc signature so Apple Silicon does not call the downloaded app "damaged" — `[package.metadata.packager.macos] signing-identity = "-"` in heca/Cargo.toml (cargo-packager signs the .app and .dmg with `codesign --force -s - --options runtime --timestamp`, verified that codesign accepts these flags ad-hoc; notarization is skipped without credentials). Worktree /Users/antonio/projects/heca-feat-566 (branch fix/t566-adhoc-sign). Then: verify with a new test tag (needs Antonio's ok — publishes a release), delete the test releases v0.1.0-1 (+ the new one) as the plan says (irreversible — Antonio's ok), close T566.

tasks.title: Findings from using the installed app (2026-11-19): fix and investigate each point
tasks.description:
Antonio tested heca installed from the v0.1.0-1 test release (.dmg, launched from the Dock) on 2026-11-19. Every point below with what was checked (file:line) and his decision. Work it in a new session, one point at a time, verifying by running; each fix centralized and in THE SYNTAX (CLAUDE.md).

1. DELETE THE CURRENT WORKSPACE — DO. `delete_workspace` exists but requires `ws_idx` (heca/src/actions/builtins/workspace.rs ~37-40); its only key is `d` inside the workspaces dock surface (keybindings.default.toml:869). No palette/shortcut way to delete the current one. Precedent: collapse_current_workspace. Prefer making ws_idx optional (default: the current workspace) over a second action; default key binding + palette reachable.
2. TERMINAL ICON GLYPHS RENDER WRONG — INVESTIGATE. Claude Code's round status dots (e.g. ⏺/●) render as green squares in heca, round in Ghostty (screenshots 2026-11-19). heca-renderer loads system fonts via cosmic_text::FontSystem::new() (heca-renderer/src/font.rs:34), so not a plain missing font: find how that codepoint is drawn (block/box-drawing path? fallback choice?).
3. PASTE IN THE TERMINAL'S RIGHT-CLICK MENU — DO. paste_clipboard exists on Super+v, Ctrl+Shift+v, prefix+Shift+p (keybindings.default.toml:252); add it to the terminal context menu (declared on the widget, the menu system in docs/widgets.md Menus).
4. macOS "heca was prevented from modifying apps" — NO ACTION. Raised when `brew upgrade` run inside heca updated apps in /Applications; macOS attributes it to the hosting terminal (App Management privacy). Document it in the release notes / docs if useful.
5. ZOOM A SPLIT PANE — ANALYZE. The header zoom button runs zoom_column (heca/src/chrome/panes/pane_items/buttons.rs ~339-347): it widens the column; a pane in a split column stays cut vertically. Float could stand in but limits many commands. Need a design for "zoom this pane" (fill the viewport, restore after) — bring options to Antonio.
6. WHERE THE DEFAULT SESSION IS CREATED WHEN LAUNCHED FROM THE ICON — ANSWER AND FIX IF NEEDED. Plain `heca` sends ClientMsg::Attach (heca/src/client/mod.rs ~157): it attaches to the most recent session of the default server — which is why the test sessions ~/tmp/prova-a and ~/tmp/prova-b (heca.sessions.json, default server) show up. When no session exists the server creates one in its own current folder; an app started from the Finder/Dock has cwd "/" (to verify) — the default should be the home folder. Verify and fix centrally.
7. FIT THE COLUMNS INTO THE VIEWPORT — STUDY. No such command today. Study a command that resizes the visible workspace's columns so they all fit the viewport (niri-like), and how it relates to zoom.
8. zsh AUTOSUGGESTIONS / SYNTAX HIGHLIGHTING NOT SHOWN — VERIFY. Plugins load through oh-my-zsh (~/.zshrc:15: zsh-autosuggestions, zsh-syntax-highlighting, fast-syntax-highlighting); they work in Ghostty. Check: suggestion colour (fg=8, bright black) vs heca's theme background; heca's ZDOTDIR wrapper (heca/assets/shell-integration/zsh/) and the login-shell change of T566; also the TAB-COMPLETION CURSOR BUG: typing `c` then Tab shows the completion list but the cursor lands one cell past the `c` (screenshot 2026-11-19) — a width/cursor-position mismatch in the terminal, possibly the same cause as the earlier "[zs]" characters.
   More (Antonio, 2026-11-19, screenshot #64): characters left on the prompt line that cannot be deleted, after a suggestion (suggestions now work only at times) or a Tab — the prompt shows `❯ --` with the cursor after it and a ghost `– antonio 2–` further right that Backspace does not remove. Same family as the cursor bug above: what heca draws and where the shell thinks the cursor is disagree (character widths / cursor moves). Reproduce with zsh-autosuggestions and compare cell by cell with Ghostty.
9. AGENT FINISHED IN AN UNFOCUSED PANE ON ANOTHER WORKSPACE, NO FEEDBACK — INVESTIGATE. Claude finished (/planner load) with no sound and no flash. Check: heca's hooks are absent from ~/.claude/settings.json (integration installed? how claude was started — typed in the shell vs the catalog); and the T562 flash change (a booked flash wake lapses when its row is not painted — heca-grid-ui/src/flash/mod.rs) must not suppress the attention feedback for a row on another workspace; sound must play regardless.
10. TRANSPARENT LOGO — DONE in PR #325 (heca/assets/icon/heca.png from heca-web/assets/logo-heca.png, heca.icns regenerated; verified the .icns corner is transparent).
11. DROP A FILE ON THE TERMINAL — DO. Not implemented at all: no WindowEvent::DroppedFile / HoveredFile handling in heca/src. Dropping a file on a terminal pastes its path (shell-quoted), like other terminals; an image could later be pasted as an image (decide with Antonio). Also a drop target capability on the widget, not app-specific.
12. MOUSE WHEEL SCROLL IN THE TERMINAL IS SLOW — DO. Config terminal_wheel_scroll_lines = 3 per notch (config.default.toml:198); trackpad pixel deltas are divided by 20 (heca/src/app/events.rs:389, a hardcoded number). Measure against Ghostty, make the speed come from config only, fix.
   Found 2026-11-19 (Antonio: still slow inside Claude Code even with terminal_wheel_scroll_lines = 6; better in the plain shell). Cause: heca/src/app/terminal_host/wheel.rs has TWO calculations of one gesture. (a) Host scrollback (wheel.rs ~152-176) uses host_scroll_notches (trackpad pixels / cell height) × terminal_wheel_scroll_lines. (b) When the program grabs the mouse (Claude Code, nvim, less), forward_wheel_to_terminal (wheel.rs ~196-209) sends ONE wheel press per winit event; push_wheel_buttons puts round(delta) into WheelUp(n) — for a trackpad that is raw pixels — but wezterm-term ignores n: term/src/terminalstate/mouse.rs (rev 891bed3) writes one report per event (SGR `\x1b[<64;..M`), or in alt-screen without mouse tracking alternate_buffer_wheel_scroll_speed arrow keys. So the program gets one report per event whatever the size, and the setting has no effect. Fix: one notch calculation for both paths (accumulate trackpad pixels by cell height, keep the remainder), and the forwarded path sends notches × terminal_wheel_scroll_lines reports (decide with Antonio whether the forwarded multiplier is the same setting or its own). Test: a forwarded wheel of N notches produces N × lines reports; a trackpad gesture below one cell produces none until it adds up.
13. OLD CONFIG KEYS ARE SILENTLY IGNORED — DO. heca never reports a config key it does not know, so a retired key just stops working without a word. Example in Antonio's config: `[settings] confirm_close_pane / confirm_delete_column / confirm_delete_workspace` are no longer read at all (only mentioned in a comment, heca-config/src/confirm.rs:11; the real keys are `[confirm] close / delete_column / delete_workspace`) — had he written false, the prompt would still appear. Fix, in this order: (a) at load, list every unknown or retired key once in the start-up report / a notification, naming the key that replaced it (one table of retired → current names in heca-config, read by the loader; no per-field code); (b) then remove the old spellings still accepted, each one added to that table so its user is told: the kebab-case serde aliases in heca-config/src/settings/mod.rs (terminal-wheel-scroll-lines, pane-size, … ~25 of them), keys.rs `prefix_key` (211), `command_type` (122), programs.rs `icons` (88), loader/mod.rs `program` alias (163), confirm.rs RENAMED `delete_pane` → `close` (25-29), and the deprecated `[settings] pane_show_cwd` (settings/mod.rs:174, now `[appearance.expose] show_cwd`). Update config.default.toml and docs/configuration.md where they mention the old names (docs/configuration.md:325). Test: a config with a retired key loads, applies nothing for it, and the report names the replacement; a misspelled key is reported as unknown.
14. WORKSPACE NUMBERS IN THE SIDEBAR — DO (Antonio, 2026-11-19). Each workspace row in the workspaces dock shows its position, 1, 2, 3, … so a key bound to `focus_workspace` with `ws_idx` can be aimed without counting (his config binds `7` → `focus_workspace ws_idx = "6"`; ws_idx is 0-based, the shown number is 1-based — the shown number must be exactly the one a user writes, so either show ws_idx+1 and document it, or decide with Antonio whether the action should take the shown number). Hideable from config (e.g. `[appearance.sidebar] workspace_numbers = true`, default true), written into config.default.toml and docs/configuration.md. The number is part of the row component (heca/src/providers/workspaces/), not drawn by hand; it follows reorders/deletes without a rebuild.
15. ONE WORKSPACES DOCK, PLACED BY CONFIG — DO (Antonio, 2026-11-19). heca/src/app/startup.rs mounts the workspaces dock THREE times: `workspaces` (sidebar.left, :323), `workspaces.right` (sidebar.right, :332) and `workspaces.left2` (sidebar.left, :337), the last two as test scaffolding for multi-dock behaviour (letters per dock, focus between docks, two docks sharing a region). Remove the second and third from the app; the multi-dock behaviour they exercised must stay covered by tests that mount extra docks in a test fixture, not in the shipped app (check heca/src/providers/workspaces/tests/cursor.rs, chrome/docks/focus.rs, chrome/docks/host/ for uses of those mount ids). Where the one dock sits comes from config: left | right | none, default left. This is the same capability as P045(F006)/T528 point 5 (a dock's first-run region from the user's config); implement the config key there once, for every dock, and use it here — do not add a workspaces-only setting. `none` means not mounted (keyboard actions still work).
16. ATTENTION ON A PANE ROW SCROLLED OUT OF SIGHT — DO (Antonio, 2026-11-19). When a pane row in the workspaces dock asks for attention (agent finished/waiting, command failed — the flash of T522/T562) but the row is scrolled out of the dock's visible area, the user sees nothing. Show it: either an edge indicator on the dock (above/below, pointing where the row is) that scrolls the row into view when clicked, or a notification whose click focuses that pane. Decide the form with Antonio; the scroll-into-view belongs to ScrollRegion (heca-grid-ui), not to the dock. Relates to point 9 (feedback for a pane on another workspace).
17. NEW PANE STARTS IN THE ASKER'S FOLDER — DO (Antonio, 2026-11-19). Today every new pane starts with no folder: split_horizontal / split_vertical / add_column_to_workspace / create_workspace all call with_shell (heca/src/server/handlers/add.rs:10-17) → Terminals::start_shell with `cwd: None` (heca/src/server/terminals.rs:37-46), so the shell starts in the default folder, not where the user was. Wanted: a pane made from a pane (split, new column, add pane) starts in that pane's current directory (the cwd heca already tracks from OSC 7 / the process, PaneFacts.cwd), falling back to the home folder when unknown or gone (shell_start_dir already falls back with a notice, terminals.rs:62). One place: with_shell takes the asker's cwd; every caller gets it. Decide with Antonio for create_workspace (asker's folder or the session's project folder).

Not in this task: signing/notarization (idea I025 area); the "damaged" message on Apple Silicon needs at least an ad-hoc signature (codesign -s -) in the release workflow — raise with Antonio as part of T566 follow-up.
tasks.notes:
18. TYPING IN THE TERMINAL LAGS — MEASURE, THEN FIX (Antonio, 2026-11-19). Installed app (/Applications/heca.app, the v0.1.0-1 release build: `cargo build -p heca --release`, .github/workflows/release.yml:72 — optimized, so not a debug build), in ANY terminal (a plain shell too), noticed today with ~12 panes across 3 workspaces. So it grows with the number of panes: suspect work per keystroke or per output wake that touches every pane instead of the one that changed (every terminal's layer repainted, the chrome tree rebuilt, every sidebar row's effects re-run, every pane's snapshot sent from server to client). Do NOT guess (memory: instrument before fixing): time one keystroke end to end — key event → sent to the server → PTY write → output read → snapshot/change sent to the window → frame drawn — with 1 pane and with 12, and count what each frame redraws/rebuilds. Fix the step that scales with pane count, centrally; add a test that a keystroke in one pane does no work for the others. Antonio 2026-11-19: do this point FIRST when T567 starts.
19. THE TOP BAR SAYS CLEARLY WHICH WORKSPACE AND WHICH PANE ARE CURRENT — DO (Antonio, 2026-11-19). Today the top bar (built in heca/src/chrome/window/scene/mod.rs; region `bar.top`, `[settings] show_top_bar`) shows only a sidebar toggle and a small cwd tab (screenshot #66: a folder icon and `~`). Show the current workspace (its name, and its number once point 14 adds numbers) and the current pane (its name / program, as the pane header and the sidebar row name it — reuse PaneName and the pane facts, never a second spelling). Composed in THE SYNTAX from existing widgets, theme-driven, updating in place from the chrome store signals (active workspace, active pane, pane name) without a chrome rebuild; observable through the existing ChromeEvents (pane.active.changed, pane.name.changed). Agree the exact look with Antonio before building.
20. THE WINDOW TITLE BELONGS TO THE PROGRAM THAT RUNS HECA — DO (asked by heca-pro via Antonio, 2026-11-19). heca/src/app/startup.rs:212 writes `.with_title("heca")` in code; a program built on heca (heca-pro: `heca::extension("heca-pro")`) cannot change it and should show "Heca Pro". Facts: once a window attaches to a session its title is replaced by `[settings.session_text] window_title = "{folder}"` / `window_title_numbered` (config.default.toml:259-260, applied in heca/src/client/mod.rs:168/269 via server::sessions::window_title) — so the literal "heca" is the title before attach (and wherever {folder} is empty); on macOS the menu-bar/Dock name comes from the app bundle (cargo-packager config), not this string. Wanted: the program running heca gives its display name once (its text from the program's own language file, never a literal in heca), plain heca keeps "heca"; the startup title and any title format that mentions the app use it (consider an `{app}` placeholder in window_title). Shape and name agreed with Antonio before code; no literal "heca" left in startup.rs.
21. COLOURED WORKSPACE ROWS, AND A COLOUR PER WORKSPACE FROM ITS MENU — DO (Antonio, 2026-11-19; he had added it from the web UI, whose task edit does not save). In the workspaces dock each workspace's rows (the workspace row and its pane rows) can be tinted with light but distinct tones, so workspaces are told apart at a glance. (a) Config switch, off/on, e.g. `[settings.workspace] coloured = true` — put it in ONE table together with point 14's numbers switch (point 14 suggested `[appearance.sidebar] workspace_numbers`; agree one place for both with Antonio), written into config.default.toml and docs/configuration.md. (b) The tones come from the theme (a palette of light tints, assigned by workspace position; never literals), so a theme reload changes them. (c) The workspace row's context menu offers "Change colour…", which opens a colour picker; the chosen colour is kept with the workspace (session state, saved with the session — T527 JSON) and wins over the automatic tone; a "use automatic colour" entry clears it. There is NO colour-picker widget in heca-grid-ui today (none in docs/widgets.md or the library) — it is a new library widget (generic, theme-driven, composed with Grid of swatch Buttons per THE SYNTAX), proposed and agreed before building. The tint is a Row variant/builder fed by the colour (no hand-set background at the call site — same rule as the pane card look), reaches plugins/RPC (an action `set_workspace_color { ws_idx, color }` / clear, reachable from key, palette and RPC), and updates in place without rebuilding the dock.
22. HECA STARTED INSIDE HECA: THE ZSH INTEGRATION RECURSES, NO FOLDER EVER ARRIVES — DO (found 2026-11-19 during T570's eye-check; Antonio approved adding it). Run heca (or heca-pro) from a terminal inside heca: every pane prints `…/heca/runtime/shell-integration/zsh/.zshenv:7: job table full or recursion limit exceeded`, the shell integration never runs, no OSC 7 / OSC 133 reach heca, so no cwd (sidebar folder line, header location chip, exposé card) and no command status. Cause: the parent terminal's environment carries ZDOTDIR = heca's integration folder; the nested heca records it as the user's own (`cmd.env("OLD_ZDOTDIR", old_zdotdir)`, heca-core/src/backend/terminal/pty.rs:366), and the integration's .zshenv (lines 3-7: `_heca_user="${OLD_ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}"` … `source "$_heca_user/.zshenv"`) then sources itself forever. Screenshot #66 (heca-pro started from heca) shows the same error. Fix centrally in the PTY spawn: never take heca's own integration folder as the user's ZDOTDIR (when the inherited ZDOTDIR is heca's integration dir, use the user's real one — the inherited OLD_ZDOTDIR if heca set it, else unset → $HOME); the .zshenv guards against sourcing itself too. Test: spawning with ZDOTDIR already pointing at the integration folder starts a shell without the error and reports its cwd. Workaround until then: `env -u ZDOTDIR -u OLD_ZDOTDIR cargo run -p heca -- --standalone`. Likely related to point 8 (zsh autosuggestions / [zs] characters) — check whether those were seen in a heca-inside-heca shell.

checklist.title: 23. MULTI-LINE TOOLTIP DRAWS OUTSIDE ITS BUBBLE — DO (heca-pro via Antonio, 2026-11-19). `.tooltip("zsh\npane-1")` shows a one-line bubble with the text sticking out. heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/tooltip.rs:108-113 `bubble_size` measures by hand: chars × MONO_ADVANCE_RATIO wide, one MONO_LINE_RATIO line tall, PAD_X/PAD_Y constants — a newline is never measured and the bubble is hand-painted. Fix the class, not the count: the bubble is composed (a Surface holding a Label, sized by the layout engine, wrapping like a Label, padding from a theme step), so any text fits; no measure or pixel constant left in tooltip.rs. Eye-check a 1-line and a 2-line tip.

23b. THE TOOLTIP TAKES A WIDGET TOO — DO with 23 (heca-pro via Antonio, 2026-11-19). The same `.tooltip(..)` door (TooltipExt::tooltip, heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/tooltip.rs; today Tip.text is a Signal<String>) also takes a widget/tree as the bubble's content — heca-pro wants a segmented Tag (program │ model │ folder). Text stays the simple case: it becomes the default content, a Label, once 23 makes the bubble a composed Surface. One door through an `impl Into<..>`-style argument like `.child(..)`'s IntoChildren, never a second builder; the live text form (tooltip_signal) keeps working. Shape agreed with Antonio before code.
